==================================================
1. FINAL APPLICATION GOAL
==================================================

I want this to behave as ONE complete working Support Ticket Management Portal.

I do NOT want the final demo to require:

Frontend → one port
Backend → another port

The evaluator should be able to run the application and open:

http://localhost:9000

and see the complete Support Ticket Management System portal.

Target architecture:

Browser
   |
   v
http://localhost:9000
   |
   +-- React/Vite UI
   +-- Spring Boot REST API
   +-- PostgreSQL

React + Vite remains the frontend technology.

For the final/demo build, React must be compiled and served by Spring Boot.

There must be only ONE runtime application/port for the final demo.

Do NOT use any port in the 8000 range.

Final application port:

9000

Do not introduce another production/runtime frontend server.

==================================================
2. EXISTING PRODUCT RULES — DO NOT CHANGE
==================================================

Follow the existing specifications exactly.

New tickets:

- always start as OPEN
- client cannot choose initial status

Only these status transitions are allowed:

OPEN -> IN_PROGRESS
IN_PROGRESS -> RESOLVED
RESOLVED -> CLOSED
OPEN -> CANCELLED
IN_PROGRESS -> CANCELLED

Every other transition is invalid.

This includes:

- same-status transitions
- reopening CLOSED
- reopening CANCELLED
- reopening RESOLVED
- skipping states
- any transition not explicitly listed above

Illegal transitions must be rejected by the BACKEND.

Field update operation must NOT change status.

Status changes must use the dedicated status operation.

Existing product decisions must remain unchanged:

- title
- description
- priority
- optional assignee
- comments
- keyword search
- status filtering
- PostgreSQL persistence
- H2 testing where specified
- backend validation
- meaningful UI errors
- no authentication
- no users/RBAC
- no pagination
- no Kafka
- no Redis
- no microservices
- no attachments
- no notifications
- no SLA
- no audit system
- no unrelated features

Do not invent additional product requirements.

==================================================
3. BACKEND — MAKE IT FULLY WORKING
==================================================

Inspect the existing backend before modifying it.

Make sure Spring Boot runs on:

http://localhost:9000

Verify all APIs against spec/api-contract.md.

Verify:

- create ticket
- list tickets
- get ticket
- update ticket fields
- change assignee
- add comments
- list comments
- keyword search
- status filter
- backend validation
- state transitions
- error responses

Verify the backend state machine is enforced in the domain/service layer and NOT only in the UI.

Verify:

valid transition → succeeds

invalid transition → 409

invalid transition → ticket remains unchanged

validation error → 400

missing ticket → 404

Do not expose database internals or stack traces to the UI.

Keep the existing documented Problem Details error structure.

==================================================
4. DATABASE
==================================================

PostgreSQL is the runtime application database.

H2 remains available for tests where specified.

Make local database configuration easy to configure through environment variables/configuration.

Do not commit:

- passwords
- API keys
- credentials
- secrets

Check .gitignore as well.

The application must persist tickets and comments across application restart.

==================================================
13. ERROR HANDLING
==================================================

Do not use ugly browser alerts for normal application errors.

Create a consistent error presentation.

Examples:

400:
"Please check the highlighted fields."

404:
"Ticket not found."

409:
"This status change is not allowed."

Network/server failure:
"Unable to connect to the ticket service. Please try again."

Where possible, display backend field validation errors next to the relevant field.
